related_questions.question: What are the new guidelines for blood pressure by the American Heart Association?

text_blocks.snippet: The latest major update to hypertension guidelines in the US is the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline, which lowered the threshold for hypertension to 130/80 mm Hg. This means that blood pressure readings of 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic are now classified as Stage 1 hypertension. The guidelines also emphasize the importance of accurate blood pressure measurement using standardized protocols and consider both lifestyle modifications and medication for treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: lowered the threshold for hypertension to 130/80 mm Hg

text_blocks.snippet: Key Changes in the 2017 ACC/AHA Guidelines:

list.title: Lowered Threshold:
list.snippet: The definition of hypertension was lowered from 140/90 mm Hg to 130/80 mm Hg.

list.title: Stage 1 Hypertension:
list.snippet: Systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 130-139 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure (DBP) of 80-89 mm Hg is now classified as Stage 1 hypertension.

list.title: Stage 2 Hypertension:
list.snippet: SBP of 140 mm Hg or higher or DBP of 90 mm Hg or higher is classified as Stage 2 hypertension.

list.title: Emphasis on Accurate Measurement:
list.snippet: The guidelines stress the importance of accurate blood pressure measurement using standardized protocols, including validated, cuffed devices.

list.title: Lifestyle Modifications:
list.snippet: Lifestyle changes like diet, weight loss, sodium reduction, and increased physical activity are emphasized as crucial for both prevention and management of hypertension.

list.title: Medication:
list.snippet: Depending on the stage of hypertension and individual risk factors, medication may be recommended. The guidelines suggest initial therapies including ACE inhibitors, ARBs, thiazide diuretics, and calcium channel blockers.

list.title: Home Blood Pressure Monitoring (HBPM) and Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM):
list.snippet: These methods are recommended to capture dynamic blood pressure fluctuations and help diagnose conditions like masked or white-coat hypertension.

list.title: Risk Assessment:
list.snippet: The guidelines recommend assessing cardiovascular risk using tools like SCORE2/OP and considering risk modifiers.

list.title: Implementation Strategies:
list.snippet: The AHA has released a Scientific Statement on implementation strategies for improving blood pressure control, highlighting the need for further research in this area.

list.title: Combination Therapy:
list.snippet: Combination therapy is recommended for stage 2 hypertension or when blood pressure is significantly above the target.

text_blocks.snippet: The AMA and AHA guidelines define normal blood pressure as below 120/80 mm Hg. Readings between 120-129 systolic and less than 80 diastolic are considered elevated. Stage 1 hypertension is defined as 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic, while Stage 2 hypertension is 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic.

text_blocks.snippet: The most recent blood pressure guidelines, including those from the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) in 2024, emphasize earlier intervention for elevated blood pressure and recommend a target blood pressure of <130/80 mm Hg for many patients. The guidelines also introduce a new category of "elevated blood pressure" (120-139/70-89 mm Hg) to identify individuals at increased risk for cardiovascular disease.
snippet_highlighted_words: emphasize earlier intervention for elevated blood pressure and recommend a target blood pressure of <130/80 mm Hg

list.title: Earlier Intervention:
list.snippet: The guidelines recommend earlier intervention for elevated blood pressure, moving away from the previous definition of hypertension (≥140/90 mm Hg) as the sole trigger for treatment.

list.title: Elevated Blood Pressure Category:
list.snippet: The new category of "elevated blood pressure" (120-139/70-89 mm Hg) acknowledges that cardiovascular risk increases with even slightly elevated blood pressure.

list.title: Target Blood Pressure:
list.snippet: A target of <130/80 mm Hg is recommended for many patients, particularly those with existing cardiovascular disease or a high risk of developing it.

list.title: Out-of-Office Blood Pressure Measurement:
list.snippet: The guidelines strongly recommend using home or ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to confirm hypertension and assess treatment effectiveness.

list.title: Lifestyle Modifications:
list.snippet: Emphasis is placed on lifestyle changes like reducing sodium intake, increasing potassium consumption, and incorporating regular exercise.

list.title: Individualized Treatment:
list.snippet: The guidelines encourage a personalized approach to treatment, considering individual risk factors and potential side effects of medication.

list.title: Improved Cardiovascular Outcomes:
list.snippet: Studies have shown that lowering blood pressure to lower targets improves cardiovascular outcomes and reduces the risk of heart attack, stroke, and other complications.

list.title: Early Identification:
list.snippet: The new guidelines aim to identify and treat hypertension earlier, potentially preventing the development of more severe complications.

list.title: Evidence-Based Approach:
list.snippet: The changes are based on the latest scientific evidence from clinical trials and research.
More patients may be diagnosed with hypertension.
More patients may be prescribed medication.
More patients will be encouraged to monitor their blood pressure at home.
More patients will need to make lifestyle changes to manage their blood pressure.

text_blocks.snippet: The 2024 ESC guidelines represent a shift towards earlier and more proactive management of hypertension. By identifying elevated blood pressure earlier and recommending more intensive treatment targets for those at increased risk, the guidelines aim to improve cardiovascular health and reduce the burden of hypertension-related complications.

text_blocks.snippet: American Heart Association (AHA) Blood Pressure Guidelines
The AHA recommends the following blood pressure (BP) categories for adults aged 18 and older:

Category | Systolic BP (mm Hg) | Diastolic BP (mm Hg) ---|---|---| Normal | Less than 120 | Less than 80 Elevated | 120-129 | Less than 80 Stage 1 Hypertension | 130-139 | 80-89 Stage 2 Hypertension | 140 or higher | 90 or higher
snippet_highlighted_words: Stage 2 Hypertension | 140 or higher | 90 or higher

list.snippet: Home BP monitoring: The AHA recommends using a home BP monitor to track readings.
Multiple readings: Take multiple BP readings on different days to get an accurate average.
Follow-up: If your BP is elevated, consult with your healthcare provider for further evaluation and management.
Target BP: For most adults with hypertension, the target BP is less than 130/80 mm Hg.
Lifestyle modifications: Lifestyle changes such as a healthy diet, regular exercise, and smoking cessation can help lower BP.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: These guidelines are based on the 2017 AHA/American College of Cardiology (ACC) Evidence-Based Guidelines for the Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults. It's important to consult with your healthcare provider for personalized recommendations and treatment options.
